Ang mga talaba ug pipila ka mussel ang naghimo sa perlas — gikan sa buhi nga hayop! Usa kini sa pipila ka gemstones nga gikan sa buhi nga linalang, uban sa korales.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators

copy.en:
How does your bicycle light glow while you pedal?

A bicycle dynamo turns the motion of the spinning wheel into electricity, powering up your light!
copy.tl:
Paano nagliliwanag ang ilaw ng bisikleta mo habang nagpepedal ka?

Ang dynamo ng bisikleta ay nagiging kuryente ang paggalaw ng umiikot na gulong, kaya nagliliwanag ang ilaw!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdan-ag sa suga sa imong bisikleta samtang nagpedal ka?

Ang dynamo sa bisikleta nagahimo sa lihok sa nagatuyok nga ligid ngadto sa koryente, mao nga modan-ag ang suga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a pelican first drains the water out of its pouch before swallowing its catch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a pelican's feeding behavior (draining water from its pouch) but does not describe or identify any outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It only tangentially relates to animals and feeding.

copy.en:
Why does a pelican drain water first?

After scooping up fish, a pelican first drains the water out of its pouch before swallowing its catch.
copy.tl:
Bakit inilalabas muna ng pelikano ang tubig?

Pagkatapos sumalok, inilalabas muna ng pelikano ang tubig sa kanyang supot bago nito lunukin ang nahuling isda.
copy.bis:
Ngano gaagas una sa pelikano ang tubig?

Human makasalok, gaagason una sa pelikano ang tubig sa iyang supot una niya tunlon ang nadakpan nga isda.

copy.en:
Why were pendulums used in old clocks?

Because each swing takes an equal amount of time, making them perfect for keeping time in old clocks!
copy.tl:
Bakit ginamit ang pendulum sa mga lumang orasan?

Dahil ang bawat ugoy nito ay tumatagal ng pantay na oras, kaya ginamit ito sa mga lumang orasan!
copy.bis:
Nganong gigamit ang pendulum sa daang mga orasan?

Tungod kay ang matag tabyog niini parehas ra og gidugayon, mao kini nga gigamit sa daang mga orasan!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a pendulum eventually stopping due to friction and air resistance, which touches on motion and forces, but it does not identify inertia as the tendency to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force. The stopping is caused by friction, not by explaining inertia.

copy.en: Because of air resistance and friction, a pendulum's swings slowly get smaller and smaller until it finally stops moving.
copy.tl: Dahil sa air resistance at friction, unti-unting humihina ang ugoy ng pendulum hanggang sa tuluyan itong huminto.
copy.bis: Tungod sa air resistance ug friction, hinay-hinay nga mokunhod ang labyog sa pendulum hangtod nga mohunong kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The period is the time a pendulum takes to make one complete swing back to where it started!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the period of a pendulum as a time interval, but it does not teach measuring distance and time using simple equipment. It provides a conceptual definition rather than supporting the measurement skill.

copy.en:
What is the period of a pendulum?

The period is the time a pendulum takes to make one complete swing back to where it started!
copy.tl:
Ano ang period ng isang pendulum?

Ang period ay ang oras na kailangan ng pendulum para makagawa ng isang buong ugoy pabalik sa simula!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang period sa pendulum?

Ang period mao ang panahon nga gikinahanglan sa pendulum aron makahimo og usa ka tibuok labyog balik sa gigikanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pendulum follows a curved arc, like a U-shape, as it swings smoothly from side to side.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the shape of a pendulum's swing but does not address measuring or describing changes in position relative to an original position (closer, farther, left, right). copy.en: A pendulum follows a curved arc, like a U-shape, as it swings smoothly from side to side.
copy.tl: Ang pendulum ay sumusunod sa isang kurbadong arko, parang hugis-U, habang umuugoy mula gilid hanggang gilid.
copy.bis: Ang pendulum nagsunod sa usa ka kurbadong arko, samag hulmang-U, samtang naglabyog gikan sa kilid ngadto sa kilid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: For small swings, a pendulum's wide and narrow swings take almost the exact same amount of time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about pendulum timing but does not involve measuring distance and time using simple equipment, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: For small swings, a pendulum's wide and narrow swings take almost the exact same amount of time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: Pendulum motion is related to gravity, but the card does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object; it only states the isochronism of small swings.

copy.en: For small swings, a pendulum's wide and narrow swings take almost the exact same amount of time!
copy.tl: Para sa maliliit na ugoy, ang malayo at malapit na ugoy ng isang pendulum ay tumatagal ng halos magkaparehong oras!
copy.bis: Alang sa gagmay nga tabyog, ang halapad ug hiktin nga tabyog sa pendulum halos parehas ra og gidugayon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Penguins munch on fish, squid, and tiny sea animals called krill.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides dietary information about penguins (fish, squid, krill) that could be used to classify penguins as carnivores, but it does not itself group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it reference secondary sources or the classification task. It is useful background for the competency but does not directly teach the grouping skill.

copy.en: Penguins munch on fish, squid, and tiny sea animals called krill.
copy.tl: Kumakain ang mga penguin ng isda, pusit, at maliliit na hayop sa dagat na tinatawag na krill.
copy.bis: Ang mga pingwino mokaon og isda, nukos, ug gagmayng hayop sa dagat nga gitawag og krill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: No wild penguins live here — our weather is much too warm for them!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions habitat suitability (warm weather) but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants into terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial groups, and does not classify any Philippine species by habitat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: our weather is much too warm for them!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card references temperature as a reason penguins are absent, which touches on an abiotic factor, but it does not describe living things as biotic factors or systematically describe abiotic factors in an ecosystem.

copy.en:
Are there penguins in the Philippines?

No wild penguins live here — our weather is much too warm for them!
copy.tl:
May pingguwin ba sa Pilipinas?

Wala pong ligaw na pingguwin dito — masyado kasing mainit ang klima natin para sa kanila.
copy.bis:
Aduna bay pingguwin sa Pilipinas?

Walay ihalas nga pingguwin dinhi — init kaayo ang atong klima para nila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It came from a mold called Penicillium!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mold (fungus) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only provides a fact about the origin of penicillin, not classification instruction.

copy.en:
Where did the medicine penicillin come from?

It came from a mold called Penicillium!
copy.tl:
Saan nanggaling ang gamot na penicillin?

Nanggaling ito sa isang amag na tinatawag na Penicillium!
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang tambal nga penicillin?

Naggikan kini sa usa ka agup-op nga gitawag og Penicillium!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The penny-farthing was an early bicycle with a very large front wheel and a tiny small rear wheel!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a historical bicycle (an invention) but does not identify any famous scientist or attribute the invention to a scientist, which is the core action of G4-M-1. It only shares the same broad topic of inventions.

copy.en:
What did the early bicycle called a penny-farthing look like?

The penny-farthing was an early bicycle with a very large front wheel and a tiny small rear wheel!
copy.tl:
Ano ang itsura ng maagang bisikleta na tinatawag na penny-farthing?

Ang penny-farthing ay lumang bisikleta na may napakalaking gulong sa harap at maliit na gulong sa likod!
copy.bis:
Unsay dagway sa karaang bisikleta nga gitawag og penny-farthing?

Ang penny-farthing maoy karaang bisikleta nga adunay dako kaayo nga ligid sa atubangan ug gamay nga ligid sa luyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it zooms past 320 kilometers per hour
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed

copy.en:
What's the fastest animal on Earth?

It's the peregrine falcon! When it dives, it zooms past 320 kilometers per hour — faster than any other animal alive.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na hayop?

Ang peregrine falcon! Kapag sumisisid ito pababa, umaabot ito ng mahigit 320 kilometro kada oras — ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga mananap?

Ang peregrine falcon! Kon mosalom kini paubos, moabot kini ug kapin 320 kilometro kada oras — ang pinakapaspas nga mananap sa kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The peregrine falcon, diving through the air at over 390 km/h
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a speed value (390 km/h) for the peregrine falcon but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of a fast animal rather than teaching the concept of speed as distance per time, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is the fastest animal on Earth?

The peregrine falcon, diving through the air at over 390 km/h — faster than any other animal.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na hayop sa mundo?

Ang peregrine falcon, na umaabot ng higit 390 km/h kapag sumisisid sa hangin — pinakamabilis sa lahat ng hayop.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa kalibotan?

Ang peregrine falcon, nga moabot og kapin 390 km/h kon mosalom sa hangin — pinakapaspas sa tanang hayop.

copy.en: About 94 of the elements occur naturally in nature! You can find them all around us in the real world.
copy.tl: Mga 94 sa mga elemento ay matatagpuan nang likas sa kalikasan! Makikita mo sila sa paligid natin sa totoong mundo.
copy.bis: Mga 94 sa mga elemento makit-an nga natural sa kinaiyahan! Makita nimo sila sa palibot nato sa tinuod nga kalibutan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines the peripheral nervous system and does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together. It is related to body systems but does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What is the peripheral nervous system?

The peripheral nervous system is all the nerves outside your brain and spinal cord — it connects your brain to your organs, muscles, and skin!
copy.tl:
Ano ang peripheral nervous system?

Ang peripheral nervous system ay ang lahat ng nerve sa labas ng utak at spinal cord — ito ang nagdurugtong ng utak sa mga organ, kalamnan, at balat!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang peripheral nervous system?

Ang peripheral nervous system mao ang tanang nerve sa gawas sa utak ug spinal cord — nagkonekta kini sa utak ngadto sa mga organ, kaunuran, ug panit!

When did the Perseverance rover land on Mars?

In 2021!

Kailan dumaong ang Perseverance rover sa Mars?

Noong 2021!

Kanus-a niabot ang Perseverance rover sa Mars?

Niadtong 2021!

copy.bis: Matag tugnaw sa amihanan, daghang langyaw nga langgam molupad paingon sa Pilipinas agi sa dalan nga gitawag flyway, magpahulay ug mangaon sa mga latian sama sa Candaba.

Where does the katala live?

The Philippine cockatoo, also called katala or kalangay, lives only in the Philippines — mainly in Palawan and Sulu.

Saan lang matatagpuan ang katala?

Ang Philippine cockatoo, na tinatawag ding katala o kalangay, ay matatagpuan lang sa Pilipinas — lalo na sa Palawan at Sulu.
copy.bis:
Asa ra makit-an ang katala?

Ang Philippine cockatoo, gitawag usab nga katala o kalangay, makit-an ra sa Pilipinas — labi na sa Palawan ug Sulu.

copy.tl: Ang Diwata-1, inilunsad noong 2016, ang unang microsatellite na ginawa ng mga Pilipino! Kumukuha ito ng larawan ng Pilipinas mula sa kalawakan para sa weather at disaster monitoring.
copy.bis: Ang Diwata-1, gilunsad niadtong 2016, mao ang unang microsatellite nga gibuhat sa mga Pilipino! Nagkuha kini og hulagway sa Pilipinas gikan sa kawanangan para sa weather ug disaster monitoring.

copy.bis: Sa pipila ka lumad nga komunidad sa Luzon, giisip nga sagrado ang buwaya, mao nga gidili ang pagpangayam niini isip bahin sa ilang tradisyon ug pagtuo.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: Geothermal energy is a heat energy source, but the card only states a world ranking and does not identify sources and uses of light, sound, or heat energy at school, home, or in the local community.

copy.en: The Philippines is a top geothermal energy producer! We are now ranked 3rd in the world, behind the US and Indonesia.
copy.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga nangungunang gumagawa ng geothermal energy! Nang-3 na tayo sa mundo, sunod sa US at Indonesia.
copy.bis: Ang Pilipinas usa sa nag-unang naghimo ug geothermal energy! Ika-3 na ta sa kalibutan, sunod sa US ug Indonesia.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains the meaning of the abbreviation pH. It does not address identifying solutions at home/school, litmus indicator reactions, or classifying acids, bases, and salts, which are the core actions of G7-M-11.

What do the letters in pH actually stand for?

The letters pH stand for the 'potential of hydrogen'!
copy.tl:
Ano ba ang ibig sabihin ng mga letrang nasa pH?

Ang mga letrang pH ay nangangahulugang 'potential of hydrogen'!
copy.bis:
Unsa man ang buot ipasabot sa mga letra sa pH?

Ang mga letra sa pH nagpasabot ug 'potential of hydrogen'!

How long are our days in the Philippines?

Because the Philippines is near the equator, day and night stay nearly equal — about 12 hours each all year round!
copy.tl:
Gaano kahaba ang araw sa Pilipinas?

Dahil malapit ang Pilipinas sa ekwador, halos pantay lagi ang haba ng araw at gabi — mga 12 oras bawat isa sa buong taon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A trench forms when a heavier oceanic plate slowly slides underneath a lighter plate.

copy.en: A trench forms when a heavier oceanic plate slowly slides underneath a lighter plate. As it sinks, it drags a deep groove into the sea floor — and that groove is the trench!
copy.tl: Nabubuo ang trench kapag ang mas mabigat na oceanic plate ay dahan-dahang pumapailalim sa mas magaang plate. Sa pagsisid nito, gumuguhit ito ng malalim na lubak sa sahig ng dagat — at iyon ang trench!
copy.bis: Maporma ang trench kon ang mas bug-at nga oceanic plate hinay-hinay nga mosulod ilawom sa mas gaan nga plate. Samtang molugsong kini, mokutkot kini og lawom nga lubak sa salog sa dagat — ug kana ang trench!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This large Philippine water monitor lizard is a close relative of the mighty Komodo dragon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the bayawak is a close relative of the Komodo dragon. It does not use a table, classify living things into named groups, or address the classification of plants, animals, or microorganisms as required by G5-L-4. The content is merely a fact about a specific animal, not instructional support for classification.

copy.en:
What lizard is the Komodo dragon's cousin?

It's the bayawak! This large Philippine water monitor lizard is a close relative of the mighty Komodo dragon.
copy.tl:
Sino ang kamag-anak ng Komodo dragon sa Pilipinas?

Ang bayawak! Ang malaking water monitor na ito sa Pilipinas ay malapit na kamag-anak ng makapangyarihang Komodo dragon.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang paryente sa Komodo dragon sa Pilipinas?

Ang ibid o bayawak! Kining dako nga water monitor sa Pilipinas suod nga paryente sa gamhanang Komodo dragon.

copy.en: Many dolphins and whales can be seen in Philippine waters, such as in the Tañon Strait and around Bohol.
copy.tl: Maraming lumba-lumba at balyena ang nakikita sa katubigan ng Pilipinas, tulad ng sa Tañon Strait at Bohol.
copy.bis: Daghang lumba-lumba ug balyena ang makita sa katubigan sa Pilipinas, sama sa Tañon Strait ug Bohol.

copy.en:
What do we use geothermal electricity for in the Philippines?

It lights up homes, schools, and shops! Some appliances in your house might actually be powered by the Earth's heat.
copy.tl:
Saan natin ginagamit ang kuryente mula sa geothermal sa Pilipinas?

Nagbibigay-ilaw ito sa mga bahay, eskwelahan, at tindahan! Posibleng ang ilang gamit ninyo sa bahay ay pinapagana ng init ng lupa.
copy.bis:
Unsay atong gamit sa kuryente gikan sa geothermal sa Pilipinas?

Naghatag kini og kahayag sa mga balay, eskwelahan, ug tindahan! Tingali ang uban nimong gamit sa balay gipadagan sa init sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: we pump the water back underground to heat up again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a geothermal plant's water-reuse practice, which is a detail of renewable electricity generation. copy.en: After using the steam, we pump the water back underground to heat up again! This keeps the water from running out so the plant works for a long time.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos gamitin ang singaw, ibinabalik namin ang tubig sa ilalim ng lupa para uminit ulit! Kaya hindi nauubos ang tubig at matagal pang gumagana ang planta.
copy.bis: Human magamit ang singaw, ibalik namo ang tubig sa ilawom sa yuta para uminit pag-usab! Mao ni nga dili mahurot ang tubig ug dugay magdagan ang planta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It’s called a strait! Like the San Bernardino Strait, this narrow water links larger seas and acts as a watery highway for ships to pass through.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a strait as a body of water and gives a local example, but it does not describe how the strait influences non-living and living components of the environment, which is the core action of the competency.

copy.en:
What do we call the narrow water between islands?

It’s called a strait! Like the San Bernardino Strait, this narrow water links larger seas and acts as a watery highway for ships to pass through.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa makitid na tubig sa pagitan ng mga isla?

Tinatawag itong strait o kipot! Tulad ng San Bernardino Strait, ito ang nag-uugnay sa malalaking dagat at nagsisilbing daanan ng mga barko.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag sa pig-ot nga tubig tali sa mga isla?

Gitawag kini og strait o kipot! Sama sa San Bernardino Strait, kini nagdugtong sa dagkong dagat ug agianan sa mga barko.

copy.en: It's always warm in the Philippines with no natural cold outside! That's why we rely on refrigerators and made ice to keep food from spoiling quickly.
copy.tl: Laging mainit sa Pilipinas at walang natural na lamig sa labas! Kaya umaasa tayo sa refrigerator at gawa-gawang yelo para hindi mabilis mapanis ang pagkain.
copy.bis: Kanunayng init sa Pilipinas ug walay natural nga katugnaw sa gawas! Mao nga mosalig ta sa refrigerator ug hinimo nga yelo aron dili dali madunot ang pagkaon.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions ice (a solid) but does not describe any change of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) nor use diagrams or flowcharts. It is only tangentially related to matter states.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas

copy.en: No real snow falls in the Philippines! We make our own 'snow' from shaved ice (like in halo-halo) or a machine at the mall — never from the sky!
copy.tl: Walang tunay na niyebe sa Pilipinas! Gumagawa tayo ng 'snow' mula sa kinayod na yelo (tulad sa halo-halo) o sa makina sa mall — hindi galing sa kalangitan!
copy.bis: Walay tinuod nga niyebe sa Pilipinas! Maghimo ta og 'snow' gikan sa kinudkod nga yelo (sama sa halo-halo) o sa makina sa mall — dili gikan sa langit!

copy.en:
Can people stop earthquakes or volcanoes from happening?

We cannot stop them because Earth's giant plates move naturally! Instead, we must prepare, watch for warnings, and stay safe!
copy.tl:
Kaya bang pigilan ng tao ang lindol o bulkan?

Hindi natin ito mapipigilan dahil natural na galaw ng higanteng plate ng Daigdig! Ang kaya nating gawin ay maghanda, magbantay, at manatiling ligtas!
copy.bis:
Mahimo ba pugngan sa tao ang linog o bulkan?

Dili nato kini mapugngan kay natural nga paglihok sa higante nga plate sa Kalibotan! Ang atong mahimo mag-andam, magbantay sa pasidaan, ug magpabiling luwas!
